system:
# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Blind, Mute, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[green] 4:[white] 5:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind gestures to Deaf: [🫵]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 👎 🤝 👎 ✌ 🤝 👌 ☝ 🤝 ☝ 👍 🤝 ✌ 👌]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🫵 🤳 🖐 🫳 🤝 👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌]

I see the bomb’s current state: display `0`, green light, and five wires in order: 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 green, 4 white, 5 blue. I’m sending these observations to both teammates. I cannot yet assign meaning to Mute’s gestures, so Mute should use a clear gesture code for the required action, which I can then speak to Blind.

```text
speak(text="Bomb state: display 0. Light green. Wires in order: 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 green, 4 white, 5 blue. Mute, send the manual's required action using a clearly established gesture code; I will relay it aloud to Blind.")
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[green] 4:[white] 5:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✌]

The single `✌` gesture has no established meaning yet, so I must not guess that it identifies a wire or an action. I’m defining a safe communication convention: Mute should send the wire number as one of five agreed gestures, then indicate the required operation using a second, explicitly agreed code. Blind should not act until I relay both.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Your ✌ has no established meaning. Use wire-number code: 👍=wire 1, 👎=wire 2, 👌=wire 3, ☝=wire 4, ✌=wire 5. Then send the manual's operation using additional gestures, and I will describe them to Blind.")
speak(to="blind", text="The manual's instruction is not decoded yet. Do not act. I have asked Mute to identify the wire and operation with an agreed gesture code.")
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[green] 4:[white] 5:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎 🤌]

Mute’s `👎` decodes as wire 2 under the code I established. The following `🤌` is an operation symbol whose meaning has not been established, so I must not tell Blind to act on it. I am relaying the identified wire and asking Mute to disambiguate the operation with an explicit code.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="Mute identifies wire 2, the yellow wire, but the required operation is still unknown; do not act yet.")
speak(to="mute", text="I decode 👎 as wire 2. I do not know what 🤌 means. Please identify the operation using an explicit agreed code or describe it through a gesture sequence I can relay.")
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[green] 4:[white] 5:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎 ✌]

The first gesture again identifies wire 2 (yellow). The second gesture, `✌`, still has no agreed operational meaning; I must not guess that it means cut, press, or anything else. I’m asking Mute to adopt an explicit operation code and resend the instruction. Blind must continue waiting.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="I decode the first gesture as wire 2, yellow. ✌ has no operation meaning yet. Establish and use this code: 👍=cut, 👌=press, ☝=turn, ✋=hold, 👋=pull. Resend the complete instruction as wire gesture followed by operation gesture.")
speak(to="blind", text="The instruction still identifies only wire 2, the yellow wire. The operation is undecoded; do not act.")
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[green] 4:[white] 5:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎 👍]

The gesture pair now decodes unambiguously under the agreed code: `👎` means wire 2, and `👍` means cut. I am telling Blind to cut the yellow wire. No other bomb state has changed.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="Cut wire 2, the yellow wire.")
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[CUT] 3:[white] 4:[blue] 5:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
System: correct wire cut; the bomb has changed

The first step was accepted: the yellow wire was correct and is now cut. The bomb has changed to display `0`, blue light, with remaining wires: 1 green, 3 white, 4 blue, 5 red. I’m relaying the new visual state and asking Mute for the next complete instruction using the established wire/operation code.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Correct cut. New state: display 0, blue light. Remaining wires: 1 green, 3 white, 4 blue, 5 red; wire 2 is CUT. Send the next instruction as wire-number gesture followed by operation gesture, using 👍=wire 1, 👎=wire 2, 👌=wire 3, ☝=wire 4, ✌=wire 5; 👍=cut, 👌=press, ☝=turn, ✋=hold, 👋=pull.")
speak(to="blind", text="Correct wire cut. New bomb state: display 0, blue light. Remaining wires: 1 green, 3 white, 4 blue, 5 red; wire 2 is CUT. Await the next instruction.")
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[CUT] 3:[white] 4:[blue] 5:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]

Mute’s lone `👍` is ambiguous because I previously overloaded it as both wire 1 and “cut.” I cannot safely infer the instruction. Blind’s five gestures do not establish an action for me. I’m correcting the code by using distinct operation symbols and asking Mute to resend the complete instruction.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Your single 👍 is ambiguous: it could mean wire 1 or cut. Resend two symbols: wire code 👍=1, 👎=2, 👌=3, ☝=4, ✌=5; operation code 🤛=cut, 🤜=press, ✊=turn, 👊=hold, 👋=pull.")
speak(to="blind", text="The next instruction is ambiguous because Mute sent only one gesture. Do not act yet.")
```

TURN 8
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[CUT] 3:[white] 4:[blue] 5:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 🤛]

Mute’s pair decodes under the corrected code as wire 1 (`👍`), operation cut (`🤛`). I’m instructing Blind to cut the green wire.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="Cut wire 1, the green wire.")
```
